newsitem.title: UK: British Airways, Air UK jets report near miss.
newsitem.headline: British Airways, Air UK jets report near miss.

text.p: The crews of two British jet airliners have filed "air-miss" reports after their planes came close to each other over Scotland, Britain's Civil Aviation Authority (CAA) said on Friday.

The incident, which occurred at 20,000 feet at 8.02 p.m. (2002 GMT) on Thursday, involved a British Airways Boeing B-767 flying from London to Edinburgh and an Air UK Fokker F-100 en route from Amsterdam to Glasgow.
An Air UK official said the F-100 had passed behind the BA jet but said both pilots had been aware of each other.
A CAA spokesman said an investigation has been ordered into the incident. Among other things, it will look into how close the two planes came to each other, he said.
On Thursday airline controllers said they had prevented a possible collision between two passenger jets which came within 250 yards (metres) of each other over southern England on Tuesday.

The incident happened as the two airliners were waiting to land at London's Heathrow airport just hours after 349 people were killed when a Saudi airliner and a Kazakh cargo plane collided over India.
Pilots are entitled to file near miss reports with the Civil Aviation Authority if their craft come within five miles (eight km) horizontally or 1,000 feet (310 metres) vertically of another plane.
